title: Cops Hunt Down Arkansas Mass Killer
description:
Submit a tip! Tips@Midwest-Safety.com

Please consider JOINING for $1 a month. It *really* helps us do original reporting like this. 

CONTACT US:
Complaints? Video submissions? Sponsorships? Collabs? Business inquires? 
Email our board at mn.safety.alerts@gmail.com. 

BE NICE:
The individuals presented in these videos may be suffering from the effects of alcohol, drug abuse, a mental health disorder or simply having a bad day. The videos should NOT be presumed to be representative of their general behavior. Everyone deserves to be treated with respect. 

RIGHT TO BE FORGOTTEN:
Midwest Safety practices the "Right to be Forgotten." If you were the suspect in a lower-level offense, you may email our board to request removal. 
Email: mn.safety.alerts@gmail.com

The suspect was a 44-year-old male who had only one prior arrest in 2011 for misdemeanor criminal possession of a weapon. Authorities were unable to establish any connection between the shooter and his victims, and no motive to the shooting was ever established. He was arrested and charged with four counts of capital murder and 11 counts of attempted capital murder. He was held without bond and pleaded not guilty. However, 13 months later, the suspect changed his plea to guilty and was convicted on all counts. The defendant was sentenced to four life terms, one for each murder, as well as 220 years for the 11 counts of attempted murder. The difference between survival and strategy often comes down to training, instinct, and the courage of a few ordinary people who refuse to freeze in the face of terror. And sadly, officers were not immune from the danger here, two were shot and wounded while dealing with the threat. And that's what separates training from theory because in the horror of an active shooter, even the ones with a badge and a gun can be cut down. Now at the 30-minute mark of this video, we see a man swing open the loading dock door creating a lifeline for dozens of people trapped inside. And this store isn't just a grocery store, it's actually the heartbeat of a small Arkansas town, and it's the place where neighbors cross past daily. And when it closed for 11 days after the shooting, it left a void that was felt across the entire community. And for law enforcement, that fact carries weight because when tragedy hits, it doesn't just wound individuals. It destabilizes everyday life of an entire town. But here's the thing, when the store went dark, the community lit up, because out of the worst kind of darkness, people stood shoulder to shoulder to prove that evil does not win. Our hearts sincerely go out to the families who lost loved ones, to the injured, and to all the families. impacted by this tragedy. No training, no words, and no after-action report will ever bring them back. And that's why law enforcement never treats active shooter training like another checkbox.
